title: Lawfulness, fairness, transparency principles
text: Personal data processing must have a lawful basis and be fair and transparent to individuals. For AI features, document the lawful basis per purpose and ensure privacy notices explain AI involvement. Treat ‘transparency’ as operational: what data is used, why, and how long it is kept.

title: Purpose limitation and data minimisation for AI logs
text: Collect and process only data necessary for specified purposes and avoid retaining extra content (e.g., chat logs) without justification. For LLM systems, define what is logged (inputs/outputs/metadata) and why. Align retention and access controls with minimisation to reduce leakage and compliance risk.

title: Retention limitation and deletion controls
text: Define retention periods for personal data and logs and delete or anonymize when no longer needed. For AI observability, create a tiered approach: short retention for raw content, longer for aggregated metrics. Retention policies should be enforceable and auditable.

title: Integrity and confidentiality safeguards
text: Apply appropriate technical and organizational security measures, such as access control, encryption, monitoring, and incident response. For LLM apps, protect prompts, retrieved documents, embeddings, and logs as part of the data security boundary. Security controls should map to threat scenarios and be testable.

title: Accountability: demonstrable compliance and evidence
text: Maintain evidence of compliance (policies, records, DPIAs) and be able to demonstrate decision-making and controls. For AI governance, keep a decision trace linking risks, evidence, owners, and mitigations. This turns privacy into explainability: ‘here is why we chose these controls’.

title: Data protection by design and by default
text: Embed privacy controls into system design and ensure defaults minimize personal data exposure. For AI chatbots, default to redaction, shortest necessary retention, and least privilege access. ‘By default’ means user safety does not require manual configuration to be effective.

title: Controller vs processor responsibilities alignment
text: Clarify whether you are a controller or processor and ensure contracts and operational practices reflect that role. In AI supply chains, document who decides purpose/means and who provides processing services. Role clarity is a prerequisite for accountability in incidents and audits.

title: Records of processing activities (RoPA)
text: Maintain RoPA including purposes, categories, recipients, retention, and security measures. For AI features, include logging, model monitoring, and vendor sharing as processing activities. RoPA is the inventory backbone for explainable privacy governance.

title: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
text: Conduct DPIA for high-risk processing and document risks, mitigations, and residual risk decisions. For LLM apps, include prompt injection/data leakage risks, retention, and access control. DPIA is a reusable decision artifact: it explains trade-offs and approvals.

title: Data subject rights operational processes
text: Provide processes for access, deletion, rectification, and objections. Ensure AI logs and records can support responses without revealing other individuals’ data. Rights handling is an operational capability, not a policy—design your storage and indexing so requests are feasible.
